newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan mulling Talisman's Wascana bid.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan mulling Talisman's Wascana bid.

text.p: The government of Saskatchewan has yet to make a decision on whether it will tender its 7.3 percent shareholding in Wascana Energy Inc to Talisman Energy Inc's C$1.7-billion takeover offer, Berny Wiens, the province's Minister of Crown Investments Corp, said on Thursday.

"We will be working with our advisers and consultants in examining the question of whether or not to tender our shares within the next number of weeks," Wiens said in a phone interview from Regina. Saskatchewan owns 5.8 million shares of Regina-based Wascana.
Its Crown Investments Corp is the government-owned umbrella organization for all businesses in which the province holds a stake.

Provincial legislation passed at the end of last year eliminated a limitation on any one shareholder owning more tan 10 percent of Wascana, a firm known mostly for heavy oil production in Saskatchewan but also has operations in Venezuela and Algeria.
A stipulation in the legislation that remained, however, was that the company's headquarters remain in Saskatchewan. Talisman has said it would add to head office staff.
It also said it would administer all heavy oil operations from Regina and establish a heavy oil research program at the Saskatchewan capital's university.
Wiens said Talisman's plans appeared to be in the letter and spirit of the legislation.

"It appears to be so and we will be monitoring to ensure that, should they be successful in their takeover bid that they in fact (uphold their commitments)," he said. "Certainly their words to us have been that they have every intention of doing that and actually going beyond that."
He said Talisman's plans appeared to fit with provincial government objectives of making Saskatchewan a major center of heavy oil and horizontal drilling expertise.
"We think this is one of the future stengths of our oil industry here in Saskatchewan and would work with any company that wanted to work with us in building that element of our economy," Wiens said.
